Definitions, scope & reproduction

Three related constructions

Moving channels use a zero-count condition. A reflection-symmetric disk containing exactly one zero forces that zero onto the critical line. The quartet certificate covers a finite interval using rational bounds. When available, the first theta-root certificate uses a fixed reference disk and a uniform perturbation bound on its stated time window. Other theta results remain numerical unless explicitly certified.

Coupling uses inverse squared gaps in a local linearization. The theta graph contains only the three tracked roots and omits the infinite remainder. Its displayed frozen perturbation is not the full theta evolution.

Newton guidance moves probes through a fixed field by ds/dℓ = −F/F′. It leads locally to existing zeros, including off-line zeros, and does not move the zeros themselves.
